set.body:
FOUND BY A REVIEWER WHO SUCCEEDED AT THE TASK AND STILL COULD NOT SAY WHAT THE NUMBER WAS.

They ran rdm() on a 100-voxel, 8-condition, 4-run simulation, got sensible values, and then had to
REVERSE-ENGINEER the estimand by hand-computing a candidate and comparing:

  mean over unordered run pairs of  sum((b_i^r - b_j^r) * (b_i^s - b_j^s)) / n_vox

Max absolute difference against rdm(): ZERO, bitwise. So it is the unbiased cross-validated squared
distance, per-voxel averaged, with K = I. That is a good estimator, correctly implemented. A user
cannot learn it from the documentation - they can only guess and check, and almost none will.

This matters more here than in an ordinary package. The whole argument for effectagram is that it
computes a BETTER-DEFINED quantity than the alternatives. Not stating the quantity forfeits the
argument.

CONCRETE STUB, quoted: ?whole_brain documents its only argument as

  normalization : Explicit frame normalization.

No legal values, no default stated, no meaning. The reviewer recovered the semantics from README
prose - 'local normalization makes every row sum to one' - not from the help page. The same
argument appears on voxels(), searchlights(), and regions().

Everything the reviewer had to guess, in their words:
  1. normalization default and meaning - Rd is a content-free stub, recovered from README prose
  2. whether RDM values are summed or per-voxel averaged - resolved only by hand-computation
  3. variation_query()'s matrix - generalized (I - J/k)/(k-1) from a single k=3 example. Never stated.
  4. measurement_frame() nodes are 1-row weight vectors, and the correlation view needs rank-one -
     inferred from a single README table cell
  5. matrix orientations for the GLM path - from one example, not from prose

FIX: state the estimand formula in ?rdm, ?contrast, ?crossnobis, and ?geometry, and enumerate the
legal values of normalization on every frame constructor. This is documentation of things the
package already computes correctly and already knows; nothing needs to be decided, only written down.

CONNECTED, and it raises the stakes on the Rd-example question that claude-review closed at pass 46:
the reviewer reports that ?plan_crossnobis is the ONLY place in the entire documentation set showing
the orientation of design, effects, and sources - and that without it, the raw-timeseries task would
have been guesswork. That vindicates the pass-46 call to close on journey coverage rather than file
count. It also means the package's most load-bearing documentation is a single \examples block, which
is a fragile place for it to live. Not an argument to reopen the bead; an argument that this one
example deserves to be referenced from the vignettes rather than left to be discovered.
set.title: The estimand is never stated: ?rdm, ?contrast, ?crossnobis document no formula, and normalization is a content-free stub
